title: How To Be A Classroom Management Superhero https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2010/07/17/how-to-be-a-classroom-management-superhero/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that becoming a figure students genuinely admire is one of the most powerful ways to create classroom leverage, comparing the effect to how much students would hate disappointing a personal hero. He outlines six traits for building that admiration: avoiding friction-causing behaviors like lecturing and sarcasm, truly listening when students bring problems, protecting students from the disruptions of a difficult few, giving meaningful (not empty) praise, sharing genuine laughter and fun, and projecting calm, decisive leadership. He contrasts this with common teacher habits—complaining, being wishy-washy, appearing flustered—that erode a teacher's standing in students' eyes. Linsin frames these superhero traits as both effective classroom management levers and a source of personal fulfillment, since teachers who embody them enjoy their jobs more and feel confident they're positively shaping students' lives.
points: Becoming an admired, hero-like figure to students is one of the most powerful sources of classroom leverage.
Avoid friction-causing behaviors—demanding, lecturing, arguing, scolding, sarcasm, raised voices—that breed resentment.
Truly listen when students bring problems, and protect students from the disruptions and distractions caused by a difficult few.
Give meaningful, sincere praise rather than loud, public, or false praise, which has a fleeting or negative effect.
Project calm, decisive, prepared leadership, since a flustered or complaining teacher is uninspiring to students.
quotes: If you’re a regular reader of this website, then you know creating leverage is critical to classroom management success.
Now what if your most difficult students felt that way about you? Think of the leverage you would have.

Keeping your cool and letting your classroom management plan do its job, however, will put you in stark contrast with most of your colleagues, and your students will love and respect you because of it.
Solving problems and addressing areas of concern shows students, perhaps more than anything else, that you really care.
Master the art of meaningful praise. Small, personal, sincere acts of praise can have a profound impact on students and is especially effective in endearing them to you.
Be worthy of a hero’s status by carrying yourself with calm confidence. Be decisive, prepared, and behave in manner you expect from them.
